pr_title: Add default rollover conditions to ILM explain API response
pr_body:
ILM implicitly configures a few rollover conditions (like `min_docs` and `max_primary_shard_docs` [source](https://www.elastic.co/guide/en/elasticsearch/reference/current/ilm-rollover.html#ilm-rollover-options)).
The ILM `_explain` API displays the user-configured rollover action with the user-defined rollover conditions. However, the implicit conditions are not visible anywhere (except in the documentation and some debug-level logging).

This PR should make it easier for users to understand the exact reasons why an index got rolled over (or not).

Fixes #103395
pr_comments: Hi @nielsbauman, I've created a changelog YAML for you.

> This looks good to me. I think the only thing that would be nice here is if we'd be able to indicate in the output that these conditions are implicit / automatically configured as opposed to user specified.
>
> That would increase the complexity here quite a bit (extending Condition to know when it's implicit and when it's explicitly configured and changing the xcontent representation accordingly - which might have implications in the UI if an accidental implicit representation reaches the cluster state for an ILM policy definition).
> I think displaying the extra conditions without an "implicit" indication (as proposed now) already adds a lot of value for users to understand exactly what rollover is ILM executing.
>
> @dakrone would you agree here?

(Github won't let me comment on the original discussion since it's outdated I guess).

While I think the implicit rollover conditions have merit, I'm concerned about what the UI is going to show. However, I think it's slightly less confusing to show them than to have them be implicit. One concern I do have is how we plan to eventually indicate these things are implicit in the future in a backwards-compatible way? Would we ever want to put them in a separate condition or sub-map? I think since this is only in the ILM explain output, it's probably okay to keep them without an indicator, but I'm also not sure if we wanted to have something like `?include_defaults` on the get-policy API to include them there.

Regardless, I'm okay with keeping these without an indicator for now, since for the UI this would only be show for a single index, and only for an index currently in the `hot` phase anyway.

@dakrone You raise some great points on potentially evolving this in the future. I think going forward as it is proposed in this PR will not prevent us from evolving the response (as it's the value of the `phase_definition` key that'd potentially be changing, or even further more, the value of a nested action in the hot phase). 

I think, if we evolve ILM to have more implicit conditions/behavioral changes, we will be able to expand the `phase_definition` representation to incorporate them in a different form/sub-map etc.

>  I'm also not sure if we wanted to have something like ?include_defaults on the get-policy API to include them there

This is an interesting idea. It'd be nice to have the notion of defaults more present/ structured in ILM (as opposed to being something we document as part of the rollover action) - if we choose to move in that direction it'd make a lot of sense to have an `?include_defaults` parameter ++ (w.r.t. to the work Niels proposed as part of this PR, I don't think we'll have issues adding the `include_defaults` parameter should we choose to go down that route)

When I started working on this PR, I was initially tempted to refactor the `Conditions` class/class structure to allow for default/implicit conditions in a more generic way (rather than just having them only for the rollover action). But I realized that that would result in quite some work (as we'd also need to update the xcontent that is used to cache the current phase into the ILM state metadata), and so I decided it was out of scope for this PR/issue. I think I'd be in favour of making that change, but it might only make sense to do that once we actually have other use cases for default conditions?

issue_context.title: Display ILM implicit rollover conditions in the explain API response
issue_context.body:
### Description

ILM implicitly configures a few rollover conditions (like `min_docs` and `max_primary_shard_docs` https://www.elastic.co/guide/en/elasticsearch/reference/current/ilm-rollover.html#ilm-rollover-options )
The ILM explain display the user configured rollover action with the user-defined rollover conditions however, the implicit conditions are not visible anywhere (except the documentation and some `debug` level logging).

This proposes the implicit rollover conditions are also displayed in the ILM explain output so premature/delayed rollovers can be easily understood.
